items.explanation: Monroe argued that east of the Mississippi, Native peoples would face endless harassment from settlers, so removal west — however coercive in practice — was presented as being in their interest.
options: A. They would escape constant harassment west of the Mississippi
B. The army would protect them on the journey west
C. They would be fairly paid for the lands they left
D. Western settlers welcomed Native neighbors
items.stem: President Monroe claimed westward removal would benefit Native Americans because

option_explanations.A: Correct. Monroe argued that east of the Mississippi, Native peoples would face constant harassment from settlers, so moving west — however coercive in practice — was presented as being in their own interest.
option_explanations.B: The army did not protect Native peoples on the journey west. Removal was enforced by soldiers and proved deadly — the Trail of Tears killed thousands — not a guarded, safe migration.
option_explanations.C: Native peoples were not fairly paid for the lands they left. Treaties were signed under duress and compensation was a fraction of the land's value — unfair payment was not Monroe's stated benefit.
option_explanations.D: Western settlers did not welcome Native neighbors. Settler pressure for Native land was the very reason removal was proposed, so 'welcoming neighbors' reverses the history.

items.explanation: South Carolina, enraged by the protective tariffs of 1828 and 1832, declared them null within the state — the Nullification Crisis that Jackson answered with the Force Bill.
options: A. Georgia defied Congress over slavery
B. South Carolina nullified Indian-removal laws
C. South Carolina nullified the federal tariff bills
D. Southern electors bolted in the 1824 election
items.stem: Nullification became a national issue when

option_explanations.A: Georgia did defy federal authority, but over Cherokee removal — ignoring the Supreme Court in Worcester v. Georgia — not over slavery, and that was not what made nullification a national crisis.
option_explanations.B: South Carolina did not nullify Indian-removal laws. Indian removal was a federal policy the South generally supported; the nullified laws were the protective tariffs.
option_explanations.C: Correct. South Carolina, enraged by the protective tariffs of 1828 and 1832, declared them null and void within the state — the Nullification Crisis that Jackson answered with the Force Bill.
option_explanations.D: Southern electors did not bolt in the 1824 election over nullification. The 'corrupt bargain' election of 1824 was a different controversy, about the House choosing Adams over Jackson.

items.explanation: As Massachusetts secretary of education, Mann crusaded for free public schools, better teacher training, and longer school terms — the father of the common-school movement.

option_explanations.A: Mann was not an abolitionist leader; that cause belonged to figures like William Lloyd Garrison and Frederick Douglass.
option_explanations.B: Mann was not a temperance crusader; the temperance movement's leaders included Neal Dow and the Washingtonians.
option_explanations.C: Mann was not a prison reformer; Dorothea Dix led the campaign for asylums and better treatment of the mentally ill.
option_explanations.D: Correct. As Massachusetts secretary of education, Horace Mann crusaded for free public schools, better teacher training, and longer school terms — the father of the common-school movement.
